technical.clientSecretHandling: Server apps send the App secret to the token endpoint (POST parameters or HTTP Basic auth). Dropbox offers PKCE for clients that cannot keep the secret, and its PKCE examples omit the secret.

refreshTokens.expiry: No automatic expiry; valid until revoked unless you set refresh_token_expiration_seconds at code exchange
refreshTokens.notes: Only returned when the authorize URL has token_access_type=offline. A refresh does not return a new refresh token (no rotation).

technical.accessTokenLifetime: Short-lived; read expires_in from the token response (Dropbox's example shows 14400 seconds, i.e. 4 hours)
redirectUriRules: Must exactly match a URI registered in the App Console
localhost URIs must be registered too, including the port

profiles.intent: Read and write files in a user's full Dropbox

scopes.name: account_info.read
scopes.purpose: Required on every user-linked app; also needed for users/get_current_account, the Stage 1 check

scopes.name: files.metadata.read
scopes.purpose: List folders and file metadata (e.g. files/list_folder)

testModeLimits.text: Development status: at first only your own account can link. After you turn on additional users, up to 500 accounts can link, but once 50 have linked you have two weeks to get production approval.

configGotchas.text: Add token_access_type=offline to the authorize URL or you get no refresh token (the default is online).
Register localhost redirect URIs explicitly, with the exact port.

stage1.summary: Self-serve: create a scoped app in the App Console, register a redirect URI and complete one code flow.

stage2.summary: Production approval is required before more than 50 users can keep linking. Review only starts at 50 linked users, and a two-week deadline starts at the same moment.

time.range: A few business days per production request
time.startsWhen: when the app has 50 linked users (or an early review is granted)

stage1DoneWhen.text: POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/users/get_current_account with your access token returns 200 with an account_id, and your token response included a refresh_token.

blockedBy.how: Freezes new links two weeks after your 50th linked user if production isn't approved, and can deny the production request.
A name, logo or privacy policy that breaks the branding guide, or permissions broader than you need, gets the request rejected.

profiles.bottomLine: Getting a first token takes one sitting. The real gate is production approval, which you can't get reviewed until 50 users have linked, and a two-week clock starts at that same moment.
topRisks: Two weeks after your 50th user, new users can't link until production is approved
Full Dropbox access may be challenged as unnecessarily broad
The app name is locked after approval, and branding rules forbid names that start with "drop"

steps.title: Create the app in the App Console
instructions: Sign in at https://www.dropbox.com/developers/apps (App Console) and click Create app.
Choose Scoped access as the API type.
Choose Full Dropbox as the access type (App folder would limit you to one folder).
Enter an app name that follows the branding guide: no "Dropbox", must not start with "drop". The name is locked once production is approved.
Click Create app.

steps.title: Enable scopes on the Permissions tab
instructions: Open the app's Permissions tab.
Enable files.metadata.read, files.content.read and files.content.write. account_info.read is required for user-linked apps and is on by default.
Save the change. Scopes enabled here are the maximum and the default your app can request.
Do this before any user authorizes: enabling a scope later doesn't change existing grants.

steps.title: Register the redirect URI
instructions: On the Settings tab, under OAuth 2 > Redirect URIs, add your callback URL exactly as your app will send it.
Use HTTPS. Only localhost may use http, and even localhost must be registered (with its port).
If you won't use the implicit grant, disable it in the App Console.

steps.title: Copy the App key and App secret
instructions: On the Settings tab, copy the App key (your client_id) and App secret (your client_secret).
Store the secret on your server or in a secret manager only. Public clients should use PKCE instead of shipping the secret.

steps.title: Send yourself through the authorize URL
instructions: Open https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=APP_KEY&response_type=code&redirect_uri=YOUR_URI&token_access_type=offline&state=RANDOM
For PKCE, add code_challenge (43–128 characters) and code_challenge_method=S256.
Optionally add scope= with a space-separated subset; if omitted, all scopes enabled in the console are requested.
Sign in and approve. Dropbox redirects to your URI with code and state; check that state matches.

steps.title: Exchange the code for tokens
instructions: POST to https://api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, and the same redirect_uri.
Authenticate with client_id and client_secret (POST parameters or HTTP Basic), or for PKCE send client_id and code_verifier.
Store access_token, expires_in, refresh_token and account_id. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token before expires_in runs out.

steps.title: Check the token works
instructions: POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/users/get_current_account with header Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN and no body.
Expect 200 with account_id. Key users by account_id, not email.

steps.title: Let other accounts link while in development
instructions: On the Settings tab under Development users, click Enable additional users.
Up to 500 accounts can then link, but the 50-user clock below applies.

steps.title: Prepare the production application
instructions: Publish an app-specific privacy policy.
Prepare an app icon/logo that doesn't resemble Dropbox branding.
Write a description of how your app uses the API, including why it needs Full Dropbox rather than an App folder.
Check the app name against the branding guide; it can't change after approval.

steps.title: Apply for production
instructions: On the Settings tab under Status, click Apply for Production and complete the form.
You can submit anytime, but Dropbox won't review it until 50 users have linked, unless you fill in Request early review with evidence.
If denied, Dropbox sends feedback and you can resubmit.

steps.title: Watch the two-week window after 50 users
instructions: Once 50 accounts have linked, you have two weeks to apply for and receive production approval.
If you miss it, new users can't link. Only production approval unfreezes the app; unlinking users doesn't.

requirements.label: Privacy policy
requirements.howToPrepare: Host it on your own site and describe what Dropbox data you access and why.

requirements.label: App icon / logo
requirements.detail: Required in the production application. Must not resemble Dropbox logos or include the word Dropbox. Dropbox may show it on its authorization page.
requirements.howToPrepare: Use the logo you use elsewhere. Size and format requirements were not found.

requirements.label: Compliant app name
requirements.detail: No "Dropbox" or Dropbox product names, must not start with "drop" or imply affiliation. Locked after production approval.
requirements.howToPrepare: Pick the final name before applying.

requirements.label: Description of API use
requirements.detail: The application asks how your app uses the Dropbox API.
requirements.howToPrepare: Describe each feature and which scope it needs.

requirements.label: Justification for Full Dropbox
requirements.detail: Dropbox checks whether the app requests an unnecessarily broad permission.
requirements.howToPrepare: Explain why an App folder wouldn't work for your use case.

requirements.label: Early review evidence (optional)
requirements.detail: Only if you need approval before 50 users have linked.
requirements.howToPrepare: Fill the Request early review field with evidence of a compelling case.

limits.whenHit: Other users can't link until you click Enable additional users.
Production status is needed for a larger audience.

limits.whenHit: The app can't link more users until production is approved. Already-linked users may keep working (unconfirmed).

blockers.cause: The URI (including port) doesn't exactly match a registered one
blockers.fix: Register the exact URI under OAuth 2 > Redirect URIs

blockers.cause: Short-lived access token, often a console-generated one used in production
blockers.fix: Use the code flow with offline access and refresh before expires_in

blockers.symptom: New users can't link the app
blockers.cause: Two weeks passed after 50 linked users without production approval
blockers.fix: Apply for and receive production status; unlinking users won't help
Use the Request early review field with evidence, or grow to 50 users

blockers.cause: Branding or terms violations, or an unnecessarily broad permission
blockers.fix: Fix what the feedback names and resubmit

nuances.text: Developer docs now live at docs.dropboxapi.com; older guides and screenshots may be stale.
Token endpoint: api.dropboxapi.com/oauth2/token (some examples use api.dropbox.com).
With PKCE, send client_id plus code_verifier and omit the secret.
Refresh tokens don't rotate and don't expire unless you set an expiry at code exchange, so store one per user and revoke it on disconnect.
Enabling more scopes in the console doesn't change existing grants. Send users back through authorization; include_granted_scopes=user lets you request only the new ones.
File content calls (upload, download) use content.dropboxapi.com; metadata and account calls use api.dropboxapi.com. files/upload is capped at 150 MiB; use upload sessions for larger files.
Key users by account_id. Email isn't a stable identifier; trust it only when email_verified is true.
If you only need the Chooser, Saver or Embedder components, no permissions or production approval are needed.
